prompt:
A cinematic storyboard sheet for a Sri Lankan television drama: 8 photorealistic film stills of ONE scene, laid out in a grid 3 panels across and 3 down, read left to right, then top to bottom. Every panel is a tall portrait 9:16 still of the same size, separated by thin, even, plain white gutters. All panels are the same scene's world, painted together: the same people, props, light and colour grade in every panel. The weather and the ground (dry or wet, rain falling or not) are as each panel says: they can change during the scene, and a panel that says it is dry has no rain and no wet ground.

Reference images, in order: image 1 is the location plate for Modern Hotel Operations Office; image 2 is the reference sheet for ChatGPT; image 3 is the reference sheet for orchestrator එක. Take from image 1: the kind of place: its ground, water, plants, structures and materials. It is ONE view of the place; each panel has its own camera position, so do not repeat this view in every panel; image 2: ChatGPT exactly as shown; image 3: orchestrator එක exactly as shown.

People (every panel): every person is a smooth, matte, faceless artist's mannequin in one solid colour, with jointed limbs and simple hands: Company A Operations Manager (Employee) is the red mannequin; Company B Operations Manager is the blue mannequin. A small raised ridge on the front of the head, where a nose would be, shows which way the head faces. Each mannequin has the person's real height and build and sits, stands and holds things exactly as a real person would. No faces, no hair, no clothes, no skin: only the mannequin colour. Everything else (the place, the props, the light, the weather) is a real, photorealistic film still.

World (every panel): Paint one storyboard image with three columns and three rows, reading left to right: eight shot panels and an empty bottom-right cell, separated by plain narrow gutters. Use smooth, featureless, colour-coded artist's mannequins: Company B Operations Manager is the medium-tall, lean blue mannequin; Company A Operations Manager (Employee) is the medium-height, average-build red mannequin. Render the office, furniture and equipment realistically. It is daytime, with steady soft daylight from the broad window on the left, warm recessed ceiling lighting, dry floors and no rain visible. Maintain warm-neutral 4800K light, restrained saturation, cream walls, honey-toned oak furniture, dark task chairs and black-framed glazing. One thin black workstation monitor on a black pedestal stands between the mannequins, with a keyboard and mouse on the pale oak desktop. Its interfaces remain flat graphics within the physical screen: off-white fields, charcoal shapes, grey connectors, teal active outlines and, only in the final panel, an amber status outline. Represent interface text areas with simple geometric bars rather than lettering. Draw no words, numbers, captions, logos or arrows anywhere.

Geography: The near office aisle leads to the central workstation, with further desks beyond it. A broad window occupies the rear-left wall, flush oak cupboards continue along the left side, and a black-framed glazed partition encloses the right side. The blue mannequin stands at the workstation's left end facing screen right; the red mannequin stands at its right end facing screen left. The monitor sits between and slightly beyond them, its display facing the near aisle and angled upward sufficiently for both standing figures to view it. Human views remain in that near aisle on the same side of the left-right conversational axis. The closer host views are taken from the visitor end of this same aisle; the inserts look squarely at the same monitor from screen height. Nobody changes position or travels through the office. The window remains the left-side landmark and the glazed partition the right-side landmark, including where either falls outside a tight crop.

PANEL 1 (row 1, column 1) — Standing eye height from the near aisle, looking across the workstation toward the rear office; 40mm, f/4, waist-up two-shot at the opening distance. Background: The broad window and window-lit oak cupboards are frame left; orderly desks and empty task chairs occupy the centre depth, with the black-framed glazed partition on frame right. The blue mannequin stands frame left, chest facing screen right in three-quarter profile, head turned toward the red mannequin, with both empty hands relaxed beside the workstation. The red mannequin stands frame right, chest facing screen left in three-quarter profile, head turned toward the blue mannequin and both empty hands down at its sides. The monitor sits between them with an ordinary hotel-system layout and an empty main content field.
PANEL 2 (row 1, column 2) — Standing head height from the visitor end of the near aisle, remaining on the established axis side; 65mm, f/2.8, medium close-up with looking room to screen right. Background: A softly blurred section of the broad window occupies frame left, with pale oak cupboard fronts behind the mannequin toward centre. The glazed partition remains farther to frame right, outside this tight crop. The blue mannequin fills the left portion of the panel from upper torso upward, its chest facing screen right and its head turned three-quarter right toward the off-frame visitor. Both arms hang down, with the empty hands below the bottom edge. Leave clear space on the right; the workstation monitor is below and to the right of the crop.
PANEL 3 (row 1, column 3) — At monitor-centre height in the near aisle, looking perpendicular to the display; 60mm macro, f/5.6, insert with a slim physical bezel. Background: The hotel-system interface fills the screen inside the black bezel; the office is outside the crop. The broad window remains off-frame left and the glazed partition off-frame right. The physical monitor fills the panel, with its straight bezel edges visible on all four sides. An off-white hotel-system interface contains a narrow sidebar, a restrained blue header accent and a vacant main content area. The enquiry card has not appeared.
PANEL 4 (row 2, column 1) — Standing eye height from the near aisle, slightly oblique to the desk without crossing the axis; 40mm, f/5.6, medium-wide view with both standing mannequins and the monitor prominent. Background: The broad window and oak storage remain frame left, further workstations occupy the centre depth, and the glazed partition remains frame right. More of the pale oak desktop is visible than in the opening two-shot. The blue mannequin stands frame left with its chest facing screen right, head turned three-quarter right toward the visitor, and both empty hands relaxed beside its body. The red mannequin stands frame right with its chest facing screen left, head turned inward and slightly down toward the monitor, and both hands empty at its sides. Between them, the inactive workflow display shows a muted central circle connected to four grey, unlit tiles, with the lower resource area empty.
PANEL 5 (row 2, column 2) — At monitor-centre height, square to the same display from the near aisle; 60mm macro, f/5.6, insert containing the entire bounded workflow diagram and slim bezel. Background: The off-white workflow interface is enclosed by the same black monitor bezel. The office is cropped away, with the broad window outside frame left and the glazed partition outside frame right. A charcoal circular hub with a thin teal rim and soft teal halo occupies the upper central portion of the bounded diagram. Four connected ivory agent tiles surround it, each containing a distinct charcoal line icon and grey text-placeholder bars, but all four borders remain grey and unlit. The reserved lower resource row is still empty.
PANEL 6 (row 2, column 3) — Standing head height from the same visitor-end axis side as shot 2; 65mm, f/2.8, medium close-up composed slightly lower to include the monitor corner. Background: The softly separated broad window remains frame left and oak cupboard fronts remain behind the mannequin. The black monitor corner enters the lower-right foreground; the glazed partition is farther right outside the crop. The blue mannequin occupies the left two-thirds of the panel, its chest angled inward toward screen right and its head turned three-quarter right toward the off-frame visitor. Its arms remain down with both empty hands below frame. The monitor's black upper corner overlaps the lower-right edge of the torso, distinguishing this composition from the earlier unobstructed single.
PANEL 7 (row 3, column 1) — At monitor-centre height, perpendicular to the same display; 60mm macro, f/5.6, insert favouring the workflow output area while retaining the slim bezel. Background: The physical black bezel surrounds the neutral-white workflow screen. The broad office window remains beyond the crop on frame left and the glazed partition beyond the crop on frame right. The active workflow remains visible across the upper screen, with a teal-rimmed central hub, four teal-outlined agent tiles and four pale-grey connected resource cards beneath them. A large, empty off-white output pane occupies the main lower portion of the display. There is no quotation sheet or amber status badge in this opening frame.
PANEL 8 (row 3, column 2) — Standing eye height on the established near side of the axis; 40mm, f/4, waist-up two-shot with the quotation monitor between the mannequins. Background: The broad window and oak cupboards remain frame left, the orderly office desks remain in the centre depth, and the black-framed glazed partition remains frame right. The blue mannequin stands frame left with its chest facing screen right, head turned three-quarter right toward the visitor, and both empty hands relaxed at its sides. The red mannequin stands frame right with its chest facing screen left, head turned three-quarter left toward the blue mannequin, and both hands empty and lowered. Between them, the monitor already displays a white quotation sheet with three aligned item groups, a totals block and a prominent unlettered amber-outlined status badge.

Bodies (every panel): each person sits or stands the way a real person does the task in front of them, never posed for the camera. The body faces the task and only the head turns: someone at a steering wheel sits squarely behind it, the wheel centred in front of the chest, back against the seat, both hands on the rim; someone at a desk sits square to it; someone at a stove faces the stove. A camera beside a person sees the body side-on, not the chest. Nobody looks into or faces the lens unless the panel says so. Head and eyes turn together: the eyes never roll hard to one side while the face points at the camera; a near-frontal face looks just past the lens.

Draw NO text of any kind: no panel numbers, no captions, no titles, no timestamps, no arrows, no labels, no borders other than the gutters. The people, place and everyday details are Sri Lankan.
